Written: 2026-11-06. The terms used in this course (modules 00–07), organized with explanations (written in Korean in the original). Details specific to a model or a paper (size, data scale, etc.) are not written here; they are in

and in each module README. The last column of the tables is the module where the term was first or most thoroughly covered. The definitions follow the meaning used in this course, and where the usage differs by field, it is noted in the remarks.
A model that is pretrained on large-scale data and then used for many downstream tasks. Even if it is called an “FM”, it does not always beat a simple baseline
The stage of first learning a general representation from large-scale unlabeled (or weakly labeled) data
The learning signal is made from the input itself (guessing masked tokens, predicting the next token, etc.)
An objective that masks some tokens and guesses them. Used by ESM-2, DNABERT and Nucleotide Transformer
Predicting the next token from the preceding tokens. Suited to generation. ProGen, the Evo family
Learning to bring matching pairs close and non-matching pairs far. CLIP, sequence–text alignment

A contrastive loss that treats the other items in the batch as negatives and solves the classification in which “the same index is the answer”. If all the logits look the same, the initial loss is ln(batch size)
Generation by removing noise step by step. RFdiffusion, the structure-generation part of AlphaFold 3
The rule for cutting a sequence into the units of model input
A contiguous subsequence of length k. It can be used overlapping or non-overlapping
Tokenization that builds the vocabulary by repeatedly merging pieces that often occur together. Adopted by DNABERT-2 (the early DNABERT used overlapping k-mers)
A vector that represents a sequence, a cell or a molecule. It depends on which layer of the model and how it was pooled
Averaging the per-token vectors into a single vector for a sequence. Check whether padding and special tokens (
An evaluation that trains only a linear model (Ridge, etc.) on frozen embeddings to see whether the representation holds the information
The pretrained weights are not updated
Updating even the pretrained weights with task data. Risk of overfitting and forgetting

Giving only a few task examples (a prompt or a small amount of training). With no examples it is zero-shot, and with all of them it is ordinary supervised learning. A setting not covered in this course
A state in which the distributions of the training and evaluation (deployment) data differ. Splitting by new positions, new families and new donors imitates it
Training only a small subset of parameters (LoRA, etc.)
Adds a low-rank decomposition matrix to the frozen weights and trains only that matrix. It reduces the trainable parameters and the optimizer memory, but the forward and backward computation remains

The order of first training only the head (linear probe) and then fine-tuning the whole. A method meant to reduce the damage that the large gradients of a randomly initialized head do to the pretrained representation†. Not run in this repository
The empirical relationship between model size, data, compute and loss. It may differ by domain (sequences)

An operation that mixes the context by a weighted sum between tokens. The standard implementation makes an L×L score matrix, so time and memory grow as L² (FlashAttention-type methods do not store the score matrix and so reduce memory, but the amount of computation is still L²†)
A CUDA implementation that computes exact attention tile by tile and reduces memory I/O†. Not available on Mac MPS

A family that processes long sequences at a lower cost than attention. Mamba is an SSM and Hyena is an implicit long convolution, and DNA models such as HyenaDNA and Caduceus use them for long-range context
Half-precision (bf16/fp16) computation + an fp32 copy of the weights. The gain is mainly in speed and activation memory
Trades time for memory by not storing some activations and recomputing them in backpropagation
Replicates the model, splits the data and averages the gradients
A method that reduces the memory of one device by storing the parameters, gradients and optimizer state split across devices†
Predicting from only the output of the pretrained model, without training for that task
A small prediction module (a linear layer, etc.) placed on top of the embeddings
Fixing a model/data to a specific commit hash of the repository to secure reproducibility
A state in which information used for evaluation has leaked into the training process (split, preprocessing, setting selection)
A split that divides train/test by a sequence-identity threshold or by family
A split that groups consecutive position intervals together (blocking the leakage of other substitutions at the same position)
A split that puts molecules with the same Bemis–Murcko scaffold on the same side. Molecules can still be similar even if the scaffolds differ
Splitting train and test by publication/measurement time
Splitting so that cells of the same donor do not straddle train and test
A cross-validation that leaves one donor as test

Fitting the preprocessing (HVG selection, scaling, PCA, batch correction) without labels, including the held-out samples. It is not label leakage, but it can favor that baseline, so the result fitted with only the training folds is looked at together as a sensitivity check
The evaluation data is in the pretraining corpus
A comparison reference method. In this course: ① one that learns no parameters, ② simple features, ③ a randomly initialized model
A model initialized from the same architecture without pretraining. It separates the contribution of pretraining. It is created fresh for each seed
Look at the score when the signal is absent by shuffling labels/inputs. A diagnostic, not proof that leakage is absent
The performance difference created by the procedure itself of picking, among candidates, the one with the highest train score
Comparing by taking the score difference of two methods on the same split and the same items
Obtains an interval by resampling the correlation unit (groups) with replacement. It is meaningless when there are few test clusters
An interval obtained by fixing the training and initialization and redrawing only the test. It does not reflect the training variation
Rank correlation. Undefined (NaN) for a constant prediction

The probability that a randomly chosen positive is scored higher than a negative (ties count 1/2). A ranking performance, separate from probability calibration. For fold models, compute the scores per fold and average
Suited to classification with rare positives.
is AP, a step-wise integral, and differs slightly from the trapezoidal area of the PR curve. The random baseline is roughly the positive fraction (depends on prevalence)
The simple average of per-class F1. Treats classes equally in imbalanced data
The simple average of per-class recall. The uniform-guess baseline is the inverse of
the number of classes in that evaluation set

The fraction of cases where the correct answer is within the top k (when there is one correct answer per query; with several, distinguish the number of correct answers found / the total number of correct answers from the hit rate of “found at least one”). Depends on the gallery size and the tie rule
The candidate set from which the correct answer must be chosen in retrieval
A conservative tie rule that counts candidates with a score equal to the correct answer as ahead of it
Fixing (committing) and recording the split, metrics, primary comparison and decision rule before producing the results
The condition that decides “supported/not supported”. Fixed as a function in code
Change only one factor at a time and see how much the conclusion changes. Not used to choose settings
The size of the difference (separate from statistical significance). Decide the minimum meaningful difference in advance
A procedural defect in the rubric that automatically lowers the score of the corresponding dimension
Getting the same result with the same code and data. Record the environment, seeds and hashes
Recommendations for reporting the validation of supervised ML in biology (data, optimization, model, evaluation)
A string of the 20 standard amino acids. Single-residue tokenization is the default
Homologous sequences aligned. Input/training information of models such as AlphaFold 2 and EVE
An experiment that measures the effects of many variants at once. It has noise
The functional/growth score of a variant measured in DMS. Its goal differs from clinical pathogenicity
Variant effects are not a simple sum but depend on each other

Scores by the difference between the log probabilities of the variant amino acid and the wild type when the variant position is masked. Distinguish it from the wild-type marginal (scoring all positions with 1 pass of the wild-type sequence without masking; cheap but the wild-type residue is visible in the input) and from the ratio of the pseudo-log-likelihoods (PLL) of the variant and wild-type sequences (expensive but extendable to multiple variants)

A matrix of whether residue pairs are close in 3D. There are studies that read it from attention. To evaluate predictions, the precision of the top L (or L/5) predictions (precision@L/5) is often used (module 02 notebook 03)
Per-residue confidence of a structure prediction (0–100)
The expected error of the position of another residue when aligned on one residue (per residue pair)
Predicted scores of the structural accuracy of the whole/interface
Designing a sequence from a backbone structure. ProteinMPNN, ESM-IF1
Designing from scratch a protein that is not in nature. A subject of dual-use review
Predicting whether a human variant is associated with disease. AlphaMissense, EVE
The genome assembly that serves as the coordinate reference (e.g., hg38). If the coordinate systems are not matched, the positions are off
A regulatory sequence near the transcription start
A regulatory sequence that raises transcription from a long distance
Open chromatin measured by the DNase/ATAC signal
Functional-genomics experiments that measure protein–DNA binding (including histone marks) / transcription starts
A supervised model that directly predicts functional tracks (expression, accessibility, etc.) from a DNA sequence. Enformer, Borzoi, AlphaGenome
One line of signal prediction that divides a sequence into intervals (bins) of a fixed width
log p(alt|context) − log p(ref|context). The zero-shot variant score of a DNA LM
A way to see the change in the prediction by changing one base
Conservation scores across species. A strong baseline even without training
A variant deleteriousness score that integrates many annotations
Single-gene disease vs traits to which many variants contribute
Non-causal variants matched on variant type, TSS distance, etc. A design to reduce the information of simple features
The effect by which a variant near a gene produces an individual’s expression difference. A different task from the between-gene differences of the reference genome
A pretrained model that predicts structure and function from RNA sequences (RNA-FM, RiNALMo, etc.)
Selecting the genes with large variation between cells
A sequence of gene IDs sorted in descending order of value after dividing by the per-gene corpus median after depth normalization. Geneformer
The property that most of the single-cell counts are 0. Biological non-expression and technical detection failure are mixed†
Non-biological variation that comes from differences in experimental conditions
Methods that reduce the batch signal (Harmony, scVI, etc.)
A cluster separation metric. Used in scib for batch mixing/type preservation
Two goals of mixing the batches while keeping the cell-type structure. Read them together
A task of predicting the transcriptome change after a gene perturbation
A single-cell model based on a variational autoencoder. Because training is stochastic, the numbers differ slightly from run to run
A notation that writes a molecule as a string. The same molecule can have several notations
A bit (count) fingerprint that hashes the structure around atoms. A strong baseline
The ratio of the intersection to the union of two bit fingerprints (0–1). For count fingerprints, an extension of the form sum of minima / sum of maxima is used†
A molecular scaffold that keeps only the ring systems and the connecting chains
Molecular clustering based on Tanimoto distance. Used as the correlation unit of the bootstrap
A kind of data, such as sequence, structure, text and images
The phenomenon in which the embeddings of different modalities sit in separate regions of the shared space of contrastive learning
An item treated as a negative in the batch that is actually a matching pair
An image of a whole pathology tissue slide
A setup in which an LLM calls tools and carries out a multi-step task
A method that reconstructs an embedding with an overcomplete sparse code to find interpretable features
A sparsity constraint that keeps only the k largest activations. Controls sparsity directly
A hypothesis that the phenomenon of a neuron responding to several concepts arises because the network represents more features than the number of neurons by superposing them
An SAE feature that is almost never on across the whole data
A control in which the same selection procedure is applied to an untrained random dictionary too
The property that beneficial research can also be misused. The scope of release is reviewed
A model/data that needs agreement to terms. An agent does not agree on your behalf
Serialization/remote code that can be a code-execution path. Only after pinning the revision and reviewing
A document describing a model’s use, performance and limitations
A document on the motivation, composition, collection process and recommended use of a dataset
Where the license was confirmed (file, API field). If it could not be confirmed, write “unverified”
Compute tier: local Mac / Colab GPU / cluster
A statement that could not be confirmed in the paper text or the official documents
Must be checked directly before use
The sources used to confirm the bibliography (the reading_list legend)
